title: Rome vs London: Which Should You Visit?
verdict: Rome for history, food, weather, and jaw-dropping sights. London for language ease, free museums, food diversity, and transit. Rome is noticeably cheaper.

categories.name: Food Scene
categories.summary: Rome wins on Italian cuisine depth and value. London wins on global diversity.

categories.name: Iconic Sights
categories.summary: Rome: Colosseum, Vatican, Trevi Fountain, Pantheon. London: Tower Bridge, Big Ben, Buckingham Palace.

categories.name: Museums
categories.summary: London museums (British Museum, V&A, Tate Modern) are all free. Rome charges for all major sites.

categories.name: Language
categories.summary: London has zero language barrier. Rome is manageable in English but Italian helps.

categories.name: Weather
categories.summary: Rome averages 2,500 sunshine hours/yr vs London's 1,650.

categories.name: Day Trips
categories.summary: Rome: Florence (1.5h), Pompeii (1.5h), Orvieto (1h). London: Bath (1.5h), Oxford (1h), Cambridge (50min).

categories.name: Safety
categories.summary: Both safe overall. Rome has more pickpocketing in tourist zones.

faq.question: Is Rome or London better for first-time visitors?
faq.answer: Both are excellent. Rome for history and food lovers; London for English speakers wanting easy navigation and free museums.

faq.question: Is Rome cheaper than London?
faq.answer: Yes. Rome runs €90-140/day vs London £110-170/day. Accommodation and food both significantly cheaper in Rome.

faq.question: Is Rome or London better in winter?
faq.answer: Rome by a wide margin. February in Rome is mild (5-13°C) with minimal crowds; February in London is cold, grey, and rainy.
